Derelict

DAIR-uh-likt -- Latin derelinquere, 'to abandon completely': left behind and neglected. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Derelict is in poor condition as a result of neglect.

The derelict factory on the edge of town has broken windows and a roof sagging with weeds.

Worked Example

A once-grand seaside hotel now stands with peeling paint, boarded doors, and pigeons nesting in its ballroom chandeliers, untouched for thirty years.

That state of ruin caused by long neglect is exactly what derelict describes. Unlike 'old,' which says nothing about care, derelict means abandonment has let the place fall apart.

How Derelict Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

run-down

run-down: shabby and worn from neglect

dilapidated

dilapidated: falling apart from age or neglect

abandoned

abandoned: deserted and left behind

Antonyms

pristine

pristine: perfectly clean and unspoiled

well-kept

well-kept: carefully maintained

How Strong Is It? — run-down → derelict → dilapidated

run-down vs. derelict

run-down vs. derelict: Run-down is a milder, everyday version of derelict -- a run-down house needs repairs, while a derelict one has been left to rot entirely.

dilapidated vs. derelict

dilapidated vs. derelict: Dilapidated is very close to derelict in force, though dilapidated focuses on the crumbling condition itself, while derelict adds the idea that neglect and abandonment caused it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — de-

prefix — de-: completely, away (Latin)

root — -relict-

root — -relict-: left behind (Latin (relinquere, 'to leave'))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin derelinquere meant 'to abandon utterly,' from de- ('completely') and relinquere ('to leave behind') -- a derelict building is one left behind to decay, the same root that gives us relic and relinquish.

Root Check

Word Choice

Derelict almost always describes buildings, ships, or land -- 'a derelict warehouse,' 'a derelict pier' -- places whose owners walked away long ago and let decay take over.
